title: PDO Database Connections
summary: PDO connects PHP to MySQL (and other databases) through one API. Use it with exceptions in development and **never** embed credentials in source control.
objectives: Create a PDO instance with a DSN
Understand why credentials belong in environment config

content.md: PDO separates **connection** from **queries**. A DSN like `mysql:host=127.0.0.1;dbname=app;charset=utf8mb4` selects the driver and database. User/password come from environment variables loaded on the server.

content.caption: Study offline — run on your computer, not in DevPath.
content.code:
<?php
$dsn = 'mysql:host=127.0.0.1;dbname=shop;charset=utf8mb4';
$user = getenv('DB_USER');
$pass = getenv('DB_PASS');
$pdo = new PDO($dsn, $user, $pass, [
  PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE => PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION,
  PDO::ATTR_DEFAULT_FETCH_MODE => PDO::FETCH_ASSOC,
]);

content.md: Do **not** commit real passwords. Use `.env` locally (gitignored) and secret managers in production.
